ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, point D is on side AB, and $\triangle CBD$ is folded along CD such that point B coincides exactly with point E on side AC. If $\angle A=25^\circ$, then what is the measure of $\angle CDE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $\because \angle ACB=90^\circ$ and $\angle A=25^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle B=65^\circ$,\\
From the folding, we have: $\angle BCD=\angle ACD= \frac{1}{2}\angle ACB=45^\circ$ and $\angle CED=\angle B=65^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle CDE=180^\circ-\angle CED-\angle ACD=\boxed{70^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, A is at the lower right, C is at the upper left, and B is at the lower left; D is located on the bottom side AB, and E is located on side AC. The dashed segments CB and BD represent triangle CBD before folding, and the solid segments CD, DE, and CE represent that after folding along CD, B falls onto E on AC. Reasoning: It is known that ∠ACB=90° and ∠A=25°, so in triangle ABC, ∠B=180°-90°-25°=65°. The folding is carried out along CD; the reflection maps CB to CE, and E is on AC, therefore CD bisects ∠BCE, and ∠BCE=∠BCA=90°, so ∠DCE=45°. The reflection also maps ∠CBD to ∠CED, and D is on AB, so ∠CBD=∠CBA=65°, hence ∠CED=65°. In triangle CDE, ∠CDE=180°-45°-65°=70°.
